1  NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB  CRL.A No. 1420 of 2017  This Criminal Appeal is filed u/s 374(2) Cr.P.C., praying to set aside the judgment dated 07.08.2017 of conviction and sentence dated 08.08.2017 passed by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tiptur in S.C.No.10050/2014 - convicting the appellant/accused for the offences p/u/s 302 and 307 of IPC.
This Criminal Appeal, coming on for final hearing, this day, Sreenivas Harish Kumar J., delivered the following:

JUDGMENT The accused in S.C.No.10050/2014 on the file of the V Additional District and Sessions Judge,
Tiptur has presented this appeal challenging the judgment dated 07.08.2017, convicting him for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 307 of IPC and sentencing to life imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC, and simple imprisonment for a period of 7 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC.

sentences.text: 2. The name of the deceased is Divyashree w/o accused.

The marriage took place in the NC:
2023:KHC:40086-DB month of Feb, 2010.

There is an allegation that at the time of marriage, PW1,
the father of the deceased paid a sum of Rs.35,000/- and gave 130 grams of gold to the accused in the form of dowry.
The husband and wife lived together at Tumakuru for about a month.

Thereafter,
the accused started ill-treating the deceased stating that he was not paid adequate dowry.
This made the deceased return to her father's house.
But the accused kept visiting the house of his father-in-law occasionally.
On 25.03.2014, there was a fair (Jatra) at Siddapura, a neighbouring village.
Except the deceased and PW1, all the members of the family had gone to fair.
Around 9.00pm, the accused came inside the house of PW1 and questioned the deceased as to why she was staying in the house of her father, took a dagger and inflicted injury on her neck.
The deceased escaped from his clasp and went inside the kitchen.
The accused followed her and inflicted NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB severe injuries all over the body.
As PW1 interfered to the rescue of his daughter, the accused inflicted injuries to him on his chest, left side of the back and left shoulder.
Then the accused ran away from the house by throwing the dagger there itself.
Divyashree died at the spot.
Some time later, one Venkatesh and Nagaraju came there and took PW1 to the hospital for treatment.
On 26.03.2014 at about 10.00am, FIR was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 307 and 304B of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. Assessing the evidence, the trial court arrived at a conclusion that the prosecution was not able to establish its case for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and therefore acquitted the accused of those offences.

However,

2 finding that there were materials to NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB convict the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 302 and 307 of IPC, he came to be convicted and sentenced as aforesaid.

sentences.text: 4. We have heard the arguments of Sri N.S.Sampangiramaiah, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Vinay Mahadevaiah, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.
5. The argument of Sri N.S.Sampangiramaiah is that, except PW1, PW2 and 3 the other eye witnesses did not support.
PW1 is an interested witness.
If the testimony of PW1 is perused, it becomes clear that though the incident took place around 9.00pm on 25.03.2014, FIR came to be registered on the next day.
There was delay in registration of the FIR.
According to PW1, PW2 and PW3 are the eye witnesses.
But they have stated that they did not see the incident.
Even PW2 and PW3 are not the NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB immediate neighbours of PW1, they belong to a village situated near to one kilometer away.
It is highly impossible that they would have come to the house of PW1 during night hours.
Therefore they are not the eye witnesses and their testimonies also indicate that they did not see the accused.
6. PW6 is the brother of PW1.
He is not an eye witness.
He took PW1 to the hospital for treatment.
The trial court relied on the testimony of PW1 to draw inferences.

If PW6 is not an eye witness and his statement is only to the effect that he took PW1 to the hospital for treatment, the testimony of PW6 could not have been used for placing reliance on the testimony of PW1.
In this view the entire prosecution case suffers from infirmities.
Investigation contains main lapses.

There is no dispute that the deceased was living in the house of PW1 for a period of 4 years before NC:
2023:KHC:40086-DB the incident took place.
The accused never objected for her living in father's house.
It is highly impossible to believe that the accused picked up quarrel with his wife taking objection to her living in the house of PW1.
For all these reasons, the accused becomes entitled to acquittal and therefore the impugned judgment requires to be set-aside and the accused acquitted.
7. Sri Vinay Mahadevaiah, learned HCGP submits that none other than PW1 was present when the incident took place.
There are no reasons to discard the testimony of PW1.
Actually PW2 and PW3 have given evidence that when they came inside the house, they saw the dead body of Divyashree and PW1 being injured.
PW6 speaks about taking his brother to the hospital for treatment and coming to know of the incident from PW1.
The testimony of PW1 finds corroboration from medical evidence.
The trial court has NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB discussed the evidence properly to record conviction.
Hence the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
8. We have assessed the entire evidence.
Among 29 witnesses, PW1 is the prominent witness.
The evidence of PW2, PW3 and PW6 may be relied on to some extent.
PW18, PW19 and PW21 are the doctors.
There is no dispute with regard to drawing of spot panchanama and inquest panchanama.
Therefore there is no need to discuss the evidence in that regard.
9. PW1 has stated that on 25.03.2014, himself and his daughter were watching TV inside the house.
Other members of the family had been to nearby village, Siddapura, to attend a fair.

In between 8 and 9 pm, his son-in-law i.e., accused came inside the house and, while speaking with his wife i.e.,
the deceased took objection for staying in the house of her father, suddenly closed her NC:
Somashekara vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192614726/
3 2023:KHC:40086-DB mouth and stabbed on her neck with a dagger.

sentences.text: The deceased escaped and went inside the kitchen.
The accused followed her, sat on her chest and inflicted injuries on her chest and neck.
PW1 rushed to her rescue and at that time, the accused pushed him to the hall portion of the house and inflicted injuries on his chest, neck, left shoulder, left forehand and back.
By that time, PW2 Venkatesha and PW3 Nagaraju came inside the house.
The accused ran away from the place throwing the dagger there itself.
He has stated that one Renukaiah, Basavaraju and Mahadevaiah were present there and saw the incident.
He was taken to hospital by Nagaraju and Venkatesh.

Later on he was shifted to Tumakuru hospital and thereafter to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru.
After discharge from the hospital, he gave a report of the incident to the police as per Ex.P.1.
He has spoken about conducting of spot panchanama by the police and seizing his blood stained pants.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama.
He also stated that the police seized the dagger i.e., MO1 and collected blood stains found at the spot.
10. PW2 and PW3 have just given evidence that about 2 or 3 years ago, when they were going towards their respective shops, around 9 or 9.30pm, they heard some screaming voices from Ballekatte.
They went inside the house of PW1 and saw a girl having fallen down inside the house in the pool of blood.
They also saw PW1 being injured and therefore they took PW1 on their motorcycle to the hospital.
Except stating this much, they did not support the prosecution case that they saw the accused inflicting injuries to his wife and PW1.
Therefore they were treated hostile by the public prosecutor and cross examined.
In the cross examination, they denied to have seen the incident.
They also denied to have given statements before the police that the accused - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB killed his wife in connection with demand for dowry.
11. PW6 is the brother of PW1.
His evidence is that PW2 and PW3 informed him around 9.30pm that his brother had been assaulted by the accused.
Coming to know of this, he came to Dandinashivara hospital.
He saw the injuries on the neck, chest and hands of his brother.
Doctor at Dandinashivara hospital asked him to take PW1 to Tumakuru Hospital.
Therefore he shifted his brother to Tumakuru hospital, where stitches were put and the doctors advised him to take PW1 to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Thus he came to Bengaluru Hospital.

When he enquired his brother,
he came to know about the incident.
12. PW18 was the doctor at Dandinashivara Primary Health Centre.
His evidence is that on 25.03.2014 at 10.00pm, he examined PW1 and - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB found 7 injuries on his body.
He gave wound certificate as per Ex.P.25.

4 13.

sentences.text: PW19 and PW21 were the doctors who conducted post mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased-Divyashree.
The evidence of PW19 shows that he and PW21 noticed the presence of 4 ante-mortem injuries and that the cause for death was due to shock as a result of injuries.
Ex.P.26 is the post mortem report.
They opined that the injuries might have been inflicted if she had been assaulted with a dagger.
However, the cross examination shows that dagger was not shown for their opinion.
14. PW28 registered the FIR.
PW26 apprehended the accused.
PW29 held investigation and filed the charge sheet.

15. If the evidence referred to above is assessed, what we find is that though PW1 has - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB taken the names of Nagaraju, Venktesh, Renukaiah, Basavaraju and Mahadevaiah as eye witnesses
, Nagaraju i.e., PW2 and Venkatesh i.e., PW3 have just stated that when they came inside the house after hearing a yell, they saw a girl having fallen down in the pool of blood and PW1 being injured.
They denied to have seen the incident.
Renukaiah, Basavaraju and Mahadevaiah are not cited as witnesses.

Prosecutor might have treated PW2 and PW3 hostile, but if the tenor of cross examination of these witnesses by the prosecutor is seen, even according to prosecutor it becomes clear that they were not the eye witnesses.
Their testimony that they entered the house of PW1 only after hearing the scream is believable.
The suggestions given to these two witnesses indicate that they came to know about the incident from PW1.
Therefore they were not the eye witnesses.
However, their testimony that - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB they took PW1 to the hospital for treatment is believable.

16. Merely for the reason that PW2 and PW3 belong to a different village, it is not possible to arrive at a conclusion that their presence at the house of PW1 immediately after the incident becomes doubtful.

They have stated that after attending the fair at Siddapura village, they were going to their respective shops and at that time, they heard the screaming voice and that attracted them to enter the house of PW1.
The reason given by PW2 and PW3 is acceptable.

From their evidence what can be inferred is that though they were not eye witnesses, they came to house of PW1 and saw the dead body of Divyashree and injured PW1.
17.
The evidence given by PW18 shows that he examined PW1 and issued wound certificate as per Ex.P25.
The description of injuries given by - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB PW18 tallies with the evidence of PW1 as regards injuries stated by him.

The evidence given by PW19 and PW21 indicate presence of 4 ante mortem injuries corresponding Somashekara vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192614726/
5 to the description given by PW1.
18.

sentences.text: If the entire scenario is put to analysis, a conclusion can clearly be drawn that none other than the accused involved in killing his wife and inflicting injuries to PW1.
Undoubtedly it was a case of homicidal death amounting to murder.
This inference can be drawn from the evidence of PW1, who stated that when the accused had brought a dagger with him.
Therefore he premeditated his act.
19. The evidence of PW29 shows that after the arrest of accused, he seized the blood stained clothes of the deceased and the accused.
At the time of drawing mahazar, the blood stained clothes of PW1 had been seized.
The clothes of the - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB deceased, PW1 and the accused were sent to FSL.
The dagger was also sent to FSL for examination.
FSL report as per Ex.P.31 shows detection of 'A' group human blood on all these items.

Therefore the FSL report corroborates the testimony of PW1.
20.
The conclusion of the trial court is that the evidence of the PW1 is believable.
As regards the evidence given about the incident, the trial court has also relied upon the evidence of PW2 and PW3 and the medical evidence given by PW18, PW19 and PW21.
It has considered the FSL report also to hold the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC.
This conclusion as regards offence Section 302 of IPC does not suffer from infirmity.

However, with regard to holding the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC, we have to state that he was injured by the accused, when he rushed to the rescue of his daughter.
We do not - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40086-DB find a situation where the accused had an intention to make an attempt on the life of PW1.
The target of the accused was his wife and not PW1.
Therefore the finding of the trial court that accused can be found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC cannot be sustained.
At the best, he can be convicted for the offence punishable under Section 324 of IPC.

Although we concur with the findings of the trial court to hold the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 of IPC, we have to differ from its conclusion regarding the offence punishable under Section 307 of IPC.

With this discussion we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is partly allowed.
The judgment dated 07.08.2017 passed by the V Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tiptur in S.C.No.10050/2014 is modified.
